subject.title: fix(browser): keep guarded CDP sockets on validated endpoints [AI]

question: Should guarded `existing-session` profiles with an explicit `cdpUrl` intentionally fail closed because Chrome MCP cannot preserve OpenClaw’s validated DNS pin across its subprocess boundary?
rationale: The patch implements a defensible security boundary, but it deliberately removes an existing attachment path for configured guarded remote CDP users; only the product/security owner can choose whether that upgrade behavior is acceptable.

options.title: Accept fail-closed Chrome MCP behavior
options.body: Keep the proposed migration error and direct guarded remote CDP users to the regular `openclaw` driver, preserving the no-unpinned-socket invariant.

options.title: Design a compatible pinned handoff
options.body: Keep explicit Chrome MCP `cdpUrl` support only after an owner-approved relay or transport can carry the validated destination across the subprocess boundary.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Land only the raw OpenClaw/Playwright CDP pinning work and track Chrome MCP and guarded-upload behavior separately.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed Chrome MCP behavior
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed migration error and direct guarded remote CDP users to the regular `openclaw` driver, preserving the no-unpinned-socket invariant.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and authored the concrete review requirements that selected the fail-closed option now implemented by the branch.
